newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch up, seen down during KGHM offer.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch up, seen down during KGHM offer.

text.p: Polish shares inched up on Monday after falling each day last week but analysts said the market should maintain its slight downtrend during this week's public offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz.

"In general turnovers are low...there's no desire to buy anything and maybe demand will pick up after KGHM's offering," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.
On Friday the Polish treasury set the minimum institutional price of the issue of 55 million to 72 million KGHM shares at 19.5 zlotys ($5.9), the retail price at a fixed 19 ($5.8).
Analysts said the KGHM pricing put it at 13 to 13.5 times projected 1997 earnings versus the overall market's current 15.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.1 percent to 15,163.8 points and turnover rose 37.4 percent to 159.2 million zlotys ($48.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 62 to 20 with 26 stocks flat.
Analysts said Bank Handlowy, the only stock for which demand was high on Monday, should gain on Tuesday and could rise toward 40 zlotys ($12.2) before profit-taking starts.
The stock started trade on Monday 8.3 percent above issue at 37.9 in a turnover of 55.8 million zlotys ($17 million).
Handlowy is one of Poland's largest firms.

Analysts said metal pipe maker Huta Ferrum's daily maximum 10-percent rise was a reaction to Friday's disappointing bourse debut 9.1-percent below issue but were divided on whether the stock had more upside.
They said Loss leader Mostostal Gdansk, down 5.6 percent in light trade, was hurt by Friday's news it had priced its upcoming share issue at 17.5 zlotys.
Analysts also said National Investment Funds (NFIs) should continue their current rises after last week's slump.
